components.name: Default button
components.description: Current compact neutral control, inverse hover, visible shared focus ring, and disabled treatment.
components.css: .ds-button { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: hsl(var(--secondary, 0 0% 96.1%)); color: hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); font: 500 14px/20px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace; transition: color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; outline: none; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / .05); } .ds-button:hover { background: hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); color: hsl(var(--secondary, 0 0% 96.1%)); } .ds-button:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px hsl(var(--ring, 0 0% 3.9%) / .5); } .ds-button:disabled { opacity: .5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Social link button
components.description: Current primary-colored social link with the deliberate blue hover fill.
components.css: .ds-social { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 0; background: hsl(var(--secondary, 0 0% 96.1%)); color: hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); font: 500 14px/20px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 4px; transition: color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; outline: none; } .ds-social:hover { background: var(--color-blue-500, oklch(62.3% .214 259.815)); } .ds-social:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px hsl(var(--ring, 0 0% 3.9%) / .5); }

components.name: Outlined project topic

components.css: .ds-filled { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; background: hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); color: hsl(var(--secondary, 0 0% 96.1%)); font: 500 12px/16px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Project detail trigger
components.description: Appearance-only preview of the current drawer trigger, including icon enlargement. Production drawer behavior comes from Vaul; accessible label coverage still needs work on icon-only variants.
components.css: .ds-detail { display: flex; width: 100%; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 0; border: 0; border-top: 1px solid hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); border-bottom: 1px solid hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); border-radius: 0; background: hsl(var(--secondary, 0 0% 96.1%)); color: hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); font: 300 14px/20px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace; } .ds-expand { transition: all 150ms; } .ds-detail:hover { background: hsl(var(--primary, 0 0% 9%)); color: hsl(var(--secondary, 0 0% 96.1%)); } .ds-detail:hover .ds-expand { transform: scale(1.3); }

narrative.overview:
A personal computing environment and an experimental portfolio in equal measure. Dense, precise information coexists with playful procedural graphics and expressive photography; neither side should be polished away.

Computing and creativity are equally important to Blake. The interface makes that relationship visible: a precise, monospace, thin-bordered framework holds an animated ASCII landscape, glitch typography, interactive wireframe objects, research details, and full-color photography. Preserve both the technical clarity and the handmade, exploratory character.

rules.name: The Character-over-Measurements Rule
rules.body: Keep the relationships that identify the site: large headings against compact information, dense panels against open graphic areas, restrained interface color against vivid photographs. Existing measurements are the starting point for those relationships, not a reason to clip content or obscure controls.

dos: Do preserve computing and creativity equally: precise information and expressive visuals belong together.
Do start from the current tokens and component consumers, then tune measurements to preserve their relationships across content and viewport sizes.
Do keep both themes first-class, including procedural graphics, borders, controls, and detail surfaces.
Do retain blue interaction accents, original photo color, and open space around wireframe graphics.
Do distinguish a protected design decision from a provisional implementation detail or approved requirement that has not shipped.
Do verify changed surfaces at desktop and phone widths, in both themes, and in relevant hover, focus, expanded, and reduced-motion states.
donts: Don't replace the protected signature features or drawer/carousel exploration model without Blake's approval.
Don't let generic component-library rounding or a new global font override the site's square-edged, monospace character.
Don't remove graphic breathing room merely to make information density uniform across every panel.
Don't replicate mobile clipping, inaccessible controls, invalid metadata, or sans-serif photo metadata as if they were approved design rules.
Don't apply stylistic filters to detail photographs or make a crop the only accessible version of an image.
Don't remove expressive motion for everyone when implementing the approved reduced-motion alternative.
